title: Typed Send is blocked for the whole Whisper download and transcription, and the ASR download cannot be cancelled
scenario: First use, or a flaky or captive network. The user taps the mic, talks, and taps stop. Whisper (whisper-tiny-ggml) is still downloading, so phase becomes .downloading(whisper-tiny-ggml) and isBusy is true. While it downloads, the typed Send button is disabled along with the mic. A stalled transfer has no time limit in our code, so typed chat stays blocked until the download ends or the app restarts. cancelLoad is only ever called for the TTS model (stopSpeaking(cancelLoad:) passes ttsModelId), so the ASR load has no cancel path and no UI to cancel it. This is a regression: on integration, Send was `.disabled(draft.isEmpty)` only.
evidence: ChatView.swift:40 `.disabled(draft.isEmpty || SpeechService.shared.isRecording || SpeechService.shared.isBusy)`. SpeechService.swift:72 `var isBusy: Bool { isTranscribing || phase == .transcribing || loadingModel == Self.asrModelId }`. SpeechService.swift:138 cancelLoad is called only at line 390+ with `Self.ttsModelId`. The inline comment says a pending transcript 'would be dropped', but transcribe() already holds it: `guard !hostIsBusy, let deliver = onTranscript else { lastError = "The agent is busy, so the recording was kept..."; return }`. So Send does not need to wait for ASR.
fix: Disable Send only while `SpeechService.shared.isRecording`, because the hostIsBusy hold path already covers transcription. Alternatively, give the ASR download a cancel action (call cancelLoad(asrModelId) and keep pendingAudio).
notes:
UPHELD(medium): I could not refute the claim. I checked it against origin/fix-speech (commits 0a2596c and 13c6130 on top of integration).

1. Send is gated as claimed. ChatView.swift:40 reads `.disabled(draft.isEmpty || SpeechService.shared.isRecording || SpeechService.shared.isBusy)`. On origin/integration the same button is `.disabled(draft.isEmpty)`, so the extra gate is new in this branch.

2. isBusy stays true for the whole Whisper download. In SpeechService.swift (under ios/AgentConsole/Speech/, not Services/):
   - Line 72: `isBusy = isTranscribing || phase == .transcribing || loadingModel == asrModelId`.
   - transcribe() (263-266) sets `isTranscribing = true` before `await self.model(asrModelId)` (268), so the flag covers the entire download and load.
   - loadModel (150-157) sets `phase = .downloading(asr)` on each progress tick once recording has stopped.
   - prefetchASR (233-236) starts the download when recording starts, so on first use stopping the mic waits on the shared in-flight load.

3. There is no way to cancel the Whisper download:
   - `cancelLoad` is private (line 138), and its only caller is `stopSpeaking(cancelLoad:)` at 397, which passes `ttsModelId`.
   - SpeechStatusBar shows only a ProgressView while downloading, with no cancel button.
   - The mic is disabled too (SpeechMicButton line 25: `.disabled(speech.isBusy && !speech.isRecording)`).
   - So the user cannot type, cannot use the mic, and cannot cancel until the transfer ends.

4. The reason given in the inline comment is wrong. A typed Send during transcription would not drop the transcript:
   - Sending sets agent.isRunning, and `speechReadsReplies` sets `speech.hostIsBusy = running` (SpeechControls line 118).
   - transcribe() line 281 then sees `!hostIsBusy` fail, keeps pendingAudio, and sets the "recording was kept" message.
   - The status bar offers "Send recording" once the host is idle.
   - So the Send gate is not needed for correctness, and blocking typed chat is a regression.

Caveat: "blocked until the app restarts" is not proven. The Xybrid SDK may report a stalled or captive-portal transfer as `.failed`, for example through a URLSession idle timeout, and that would end the block. What is certain is that typed chat is blocked for however long the ~75 MB first-use download takes on a slow network, with no way to cancel.

Severity: medium is defensible, though low-medium may be fairer since the block is probably bounded by an SDK or network timeout. | fix: In ChatView.swift:40, change the gate to `.disabled(draft.isEmpty || SpeechService.shared.isRecording)`. The hostIsBusy hold in transcribe() (SpeechService.swift:281) already keeps the audio if a typed send happens during transcription.

Optionally, also add a public `cancelASRDownload()` that calls `cancelLoad(Self.asrModelId)` and keeps pendingAudio. Show it as a Cancel button in SpeechStatusBar's `.downloading` case when the model is Whisper.

UPHELD(high): I confirmed this on origin/fix-speech.

1. ChatView.swift:40 has `.disabled(draft.isEmpty || SpeechService.shared.isRecording || SpeechService.shared.isBusy)`. On origin/integration it was only `.disabled(draft.isEmpty)`, so this is a regression.

2. SpeechService.swift:72 sets `isBusy` to `isTranscribing || phase == .transcribing || loadingModel == asrModelId`. `loadingModel` is true whenever phase is `.downloading` or `.loading` for whisper. `showLoading` only sets that phase once the phase has gone back to idle, and `finishRecording` resets it to idle right away. So after the user taps stop, the phase becomes `.downloading(whisper)` and `isBusy` stays true until the download or load ends. `transcribe()` also sets `isTranscribing = true` across `await self.model(asr)`.

3. Nothing in our code can stop it.
   - The `download.progress()` loop has no timeout. Any timeout would have to come from the Xybrid SDK, which I can't check from here.
   - `cancelLoad` is private. Its only call is `stopSpeaking(cancelLoad:)` at line 397, which passes `ttsModelId`.
   - SpeechStatusBar's `.downloading` case only shows a ProgressView with no cancel button. The Retry and Discard buttons appear only when `!isBusy`.
   - The mic button is disabled while `isBusy && !isRecording`.
   So a stalled Whisper download blocks typed Send until the transfer ends or the app restarts.

4. The reason given in the comment, that the transcript "would be dropped", is wrong.
   - `speechReadsReplies` (SpeechControls.swift:118) sets `hostIsBusy = running` whenever `agent.isRunning` changes.
   - `transcribe()` at line 281 checks `guard !hostIsBusy, let deliver = onTranscript`, and if the host is busy it keeps `pendingAudio` and shows a "tap Send" message. So a typed Send during download or transcription would leave the transcript held, not lost.
   - If the user types Send while still recording, `suspendRecording` keeps the audio.

5. There is one more path the claim doesn't mention. `prefetchASR` (lines 233-236) starts the Whisper download when recording begins. Even if the recording is then cancelled or empty, that background download keeps `isBusy` true and Send disabled.

6. The fix is minimal and safe because the hold path already covers transcription and the recording case is handled separately. | fix: In ChatView.swift:40, change the line to `.disabled(draft.isEmpty || SpeechService.shared.isRecording)`. The hostIsBusy hold in transcribe() already keeps a transcript that finishes while the agent is running. Optionally, also add a public `cancelASRLoad()` that calls `cancelLoad(Self.asrModelId)` and leaves `pendingAudio` alone, and show a Cancel button in the `.downloading`/`.loading` cases of SpeechStatusBar. After a cancel, the catch path in transcribe() keeps the recording available for Retry.

UPHELD(medium): I could not refute this. Each step of the scenario is in the code.

1. Regression. On origin/integration, ChatView.swift:39 has only `.disabled(draft.isEmpty)`. On origin/fix-speech (commit 0a2596c), ChatView.swift:40 adds `|| SpeechService.shared.isRecording || SpeechService.shared.isBusy`.

2. Blocking path. In SpeechService.swift:208-234, startRecording() calls prefetchASR(), which starts model(asrModelId). While recording, showLoading() does not overwrite `.recording`. On stop, finishRecording() (lines 240-250) sets phase = .idle and then awaits transcribe(). The next download progress tick then sets phase to `.downloading(whisper,…)`. That makes loadingModel == asrModelId, so isBusy (line 72) is true. isTranscribing is also true for the whole of transcribe(), so Send stays disabled for the full download, the load and the Whisper run.

3. No cancel path. cancelLoad is private (line 138). Its only caller is stopSpeaking(cancelLoad:) at line 397, with ttsModelId. The mic button is disabled while isBusy && !isRecording. SpeechStatusBar shows only a ProgressView in the .downloading, .loading and .transcribing cases, with no button. So nothing in the UI stops an ASR download or transcription.

4. The comment's reason does not hold. speechReadsReplies sets hostIsBusy = agent.isRunning. If typed Send were allowed during transcription, the agent would run and hostIsBusy would be true. transcribe() (lines 281-283) would then keep pendingAudio and set lastError, and the user resends it with "Send recording" / retryTranscription. If the agent finishes first, the transcript is simply delivered as the next turn. Either way the transcript is not dropped, so the gate only blocks typed chat.

Caveat that weakens "until the app restarts": I could not check Xybrid's download timeouts. A completely stalled URLSession transfer would probably fail on the request idle timeout, which then ends the busy state through the catch path. A slow or captive network can still keep a roughly 75 MB first-use Whisper download, and typed Send, blocked for many minutes with no way to cancel. So the defect is real, but medium may overstate it; it is a medium-to-low UX regression. | fix: In ChatView.swift:40 use `.disabled(draft.isEmpty || SpeechService.shared.isRecording)`. Sending while recording is already handled by suspendRecording in speechReadsReplies, and a transcript that finishes while the agent is busy is already kept by the hostIsBusy hold in transcribe(). Optionally, also add a Cancel button to SpeechStatusBar for `.downloading` / `.loading` of asrModelId. It would call a new public `cancelASRLoad()` that runs `cancelLoad(Self.asrModelId)` and keeps pendingAudio. transcribe()'s catch then shows Retry.

title: The new post-stream checkCancellation writes a stray 'Stopped.' turn into the fresh chat after New chat or a model switch mid-reply
scenario: A reply is streaming. The user picks another model in Settings (SettingsView calls AppModel.shared.agent.reset()) or taps New chat. reset() cancels the task and sets turns = []. The cancelled stream ends cleanly, so the new `try Task.checkCancellation()` throws, and `catch is CancellationError` appends Turn(.error, "Stopped.") to the new, empty transcript. The new chat therefore opens with an orange 'Stopped.' row. Before this change, a cleanly ended stream returned without appending anything, unless a tool call had been parsed.
evidence: LocalAgent.swift:36-41 reset() does `task?.cancel(); ... turns = []`. Line 152 adds `try Task.checkCancellation()`. Lines 188-189: `catch is CancellationError { turns.append(Turn(role: .error, text: "Stopped.")) }`, with no check that the chat is still the same one. PR #3 (memory-harness) fixes this with `append(to: chat, ...)`. Git auto-merges cleanly with it, so the bug exists only while fix-speech lands without #3.
fix: Capture a run id or generation in send() and skip the 'Stopped.' append when reset() changed it, or land #3's append(to:) guard together with this change.
notes: UPHELD(high): I could not refute the claim; the code on origin/fix-speech matches it. In LocalAgent.swift, reset() (lines 36-41) cancels `task` and sets `turns = []` synchronously on the MainActor. It does not wait for the run to finish or mark the old run as stale. The run continues inside that same cancelled Task, so Task.isCancelled is true. The fix-speech diff adds only `try Task.checkCancellation()` at line 152, right after the stream loop. Its own comment says that cancelling the consumer just ends the stream with no error. So after reset(), control reaches line 152, the call throws CancellationError, and `catch is CancellationError` at lines 188-189 runs `turns.append(Turn(role: .error, text: "Stopped."))`. Nothing checks whether the chat is still the same one, so that row goes into the new, empty `turns` array. Two callers exist on this branch: ChatView.swift:51 ("New chat" calls agent.reset()) and SettingsView.swift:37 (model switch calls AppModel.shared.agent.reset()). Before this change, the in-loop check at line 135 only threw if another event arrived after the cancel. A stream that ended cleanly fell through to `return` at line 172 without appending anything. The new check makes the stray row appear every time a reply is cancelled mid-stream. The impact is cosmetic: an orange 'Stopped.' row in a fresh chat, with no data loss. Severity low, as claimed. Fix: capture a generation counter in send() that reset() increments, and skip the catch-block append when it no longer matches. Alternatively, land PR #3's chat-scoped append(to:) guard together with this change. | fix: Add `private var generation = 0` to LocalAgent and increment it in reset(). In send(), capture `let gen = generation` and pass it to run(). In run's `catch is CancellationError`, append 'Stopped.' only when `gen == generation`; apply the same check to the other catch branches. Alternatively, merge with PR #3's append(to: chat, ...) guard.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute the claim. On origin/fix-speech the code does what the scenario describes.

1. Both entry points are always reachable. ChatView.swift:51 shows "New chat" with `agent.reset()` and no disabled guard while isRunning. SettingsView.swift:37 calls `AppModel.shared.agent.reset()` from onChange of selectedModelID.
2. reset() (LocalAgent.swift:36-41) cancels `task` and sets `turns = []`. The stream loop at line 134 runs inside that same Task: withGPU's body is awaited inline, not in a new Task, so the cancellation reaches the `for try await`.
3. AsyncThrowingStream iteration responds to cancellation. When the consuming task is cancelled while suspended in next(), it returns nil and does not throw. onTermination in MLXBackend.swift:153 then cancels the upstream producer, so the loop ends cleanly. That matches the PR's own comment at lines 150-151.
4. The new `try Task.checkCancellation()` at line 152 then throws CancellationError. The catch at lines 188-189 appends `Turn(.error, "Stopped.")` to `turns`, which reset() has already emptied. There is no generation or chat-identity check, so the new chat opens with a "Stopped." row.
5. On integration, the stream ending cleanly fell through to `guard let call = ... else { return }` and appended nothing. The one exception was the rarer case where a buffered element was delivered after cancellation and the in-loop check at line 135 threw. That makes this a real regression: a race that was rare before now happens every time.

The impact is cosmetic: one stray error row, with no crash and no data loss. Low severity is correct. | fix: In send(), increment a `generation` counter and pass the value into run(). reset() also increments it. In the CancellationError catch, append "Stopped." only when the generation still matches (`if gen == generation { turns.append(...) }`). Alternatively, land this together with PR #3's append(to: chat, ...) guard.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this. Here is the failing sequence on origin/fix-speech.

1. A reply is streaming. The run task is suspended inside `for try await event in stream` (LocalAgent.swift:134).
2. The user taps New chat (ChatView.swift:51) or picks another model (SettingsView.swift:37). Both call `agent.reset()`, which runs synchronously on the main actor: `task?.cancel()`, then `turns = []` (lines 36-41).
3. The cancel ends the stream. In `MLXBackend.map` (MLXBackend.swift:128-155), the consumer's cancellation finishes the AsyncThrowingStream and `onTermination` cancels the producer. If no element is buffered, which is the common case because the main-actor consumer drains tokens as they arrive, `next()` returns nil and the for-await loop exits without throwing. Line 135 never runs.
4. The new line 152, `try Task.checkCancellation()`, then throws CancellationError. The catch at lines 188-189 runs `turns.append(Turn(role: .error, text: "Stopped."))` on the now-empty array. Nothing checks whether a reset happened, so the fresh chat shows a single 'Stopped.' error row.

On integration, the same clean end fell through to `guard let call = ... else { return }` and appended nothing, unless a tool call had been parsed (line 119 at the next iteration). The fix-speech diff only adds 3 lines to LocalAgent.swift, so this is a regression, though a narrow one. A buffered-token race at line 135 could already produce the stray row before this change, but now it happens on nearly every New chat or model switch made mid-reply.

The impact is cosmetic: one stray orange row, no data loss and no crash. Low severity is right. | fix: Have `reset()` bump a generation counter (`private var generation = 0; func reset() { generation += 1; task?.cancel(); ... }`). In `send()`, capture `let gen = generation` and pass it into `run`. In the catch blocks, and wherever else the code appends after an await, guard with `guard gen == generation else { return }` before writing to `turns`. Alternatively, land PR #3's `append(to: chat, ...)` guard together with fix-speech.

title: SettingsView merge conflict with PR #2 (inkling2) and PR #3 (memory-harness)
scenario: Whichever of #2, #3 and #5 merges second or third hits a content conflict. All three insert a new Section at the same spot, right after the 'On-device' section footer: fix-speech adds `SpeechSettingsSection()`, inkling2 adds `MemorySection(ignoreMemoryCheck:)`, memory-harness adds `MemorySettingsSection(memory:)`. inkling2 also rewrites the footer lines next to it. A careless resolution can drop one section, and with it the speech voice picker or the memory override toggle. docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md also conflicts with every open PR, because they all add entries at the top of the log. LocalAgent.swift and ChatView.swift auto-merge cleanly with #3 and #6, and the merged code keeps the correct semantics.
evidence: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/fix-speech origin/memory-harness` and `... origin/inkling2` each report `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in ios/AgentConsole/Views/SettingsView.swift`, plus docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md. Merging with fix-node or bench conflicts only in ENGINEERING-LOG.md.
fix: When resolving, keep all three sections: SpeechSettingsSection(), MemorySection(...) and MemorySettingsSection(...). Rebase whichever lands later.
notes:
UPHELD(high): I could not refute this claim. After a fresh `git fetch`, `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/fix-speech` against each other branch gave these results:
- `origin/memory-harness`: content conflicts in ios/AgentConsole/Views/SettingsView.swift and docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md.
- `origin/inkling2`: the same two conflicts.
- `origin/fix-node` and `origin/bench`: a conflict in docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md only.

The fix-speech diff against integration adds `SpeechSettingsSection()` right after the On-device section footer, around line 48. That is the spot the claim names, and it also adds the `SpeechService.shared.modelSelected(entry)` call in the model picker. This is a real merge hazard, not a runtime bug. Low severity is right: a careless resolution could drop either the speech voice picker or the memory section. Note that I did not re-check the claim's statement about which section inkling2 and memory-harness each insert. | fix: When you resolve the SettingsView.swift conflict, keep every inserted Section: `SpeechSettingsSection()` from fix-speech, plus the memory section from inkling2 or memory-harness. Also keep inkling2's footer rewrite and the `SpeechService.shared.modelSelected(entry)` line in the model onChange handler. For docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md, keep every PR's entries in a single ordered sequence. Rebase whichever PR lands later onto the updated integration branch.

Also keep #2's rewritten footer text. For ENGINEERING-LOG.md, keep every PR's top-of-log entry.
